title: Research
text:
My research develops statistical methods for understanding complex dependence, variation, and change in structured data. A central theme of my work is the development of methods that move beyond inference on the underlying process itself to characterize its local behavior—including gradients, directional change, boundaries, and curvature.


This work spans spatial and spatiotemporal statistics, Gaussian processes, Bayesian computation, and statistical methodology for data observed over non-Euclidean domains.







01



Spatial processes are often scientifically interesting not only because of their levels, but because of how and where they change. My work develops inferential methods for derivatives of spatial and spatiotemporal processes, allowing local rates and directions of change to be quantified together with their uncertainty.
This perspective provides a foundation for wombling, where boundaries are identified through unusually large directional gradients, and extends naturally to higher-order differential behavior through curvature processes. These methods provide tools for detecting and characterizing spatial boundaries, directional change, and other local geometric features of complex processes.

Gradients · Directional derivatives · Spatial wombling · Spatiotemporal wombling · Curvature

View related publications →





02



Many modern data are observed over domains whose geometry cannot be adequately represented by ordinary Euclidean space. Examples include cortical surfaces, anatomical structures, environmental surfaces, and other complex geometric objects.
My work develops Gaussian-process methodology directly over manifold domains, with particular emphasis on differential inference. Rather than treating the manifold merely as a complicated coordinate system embedded in three-dimensional space, the goal is to formulate gradients, directional derivatives, curvature, and related quantities intrinsically with respect to the geometry of the domain.
This creates a framework for extending spatial derivative processes and wombling to non-Euclidean settings and provides a foundation for a broader program of statistical inference for processes observed over manifolds.

Gaussian processes on manifolds · Intrinsic gradients · Tangent vector fields · Curvature · Manifold wombling

View related publications →








03



Increasingly rich spatial models create substantial computational challenges, particularly for large datasets and complex hierarchical Bayesian models. A complementary component of my research therefore focuses on computational methods that make sophisticated spatial and spatiotemporal models practically usable.
This includes work on efficient Bayesian computation and software as well as research toward scalable Gaussian-process models, nearest-neighbor representations, and multiresolution approaches. A major direction of this work is to connect scalable computation with the derivative and geometric inference developed elsewhere in my research program.

Bayesian computation · Scalable Gaussian processes · Nearest-neighbor methods · Multiresolution models · Statistical software

View software →    View related publications →





04



Methodological development in my research is motivated by scientific problems in which spatial structure, local change, geometry, or computational scale plays an important role.
Applications of this work span environmental and ecological science, public health, and biomedical settings. These collaborations provide both substantive scientific questions and new methodological challenges, particularly when conventional spatial domains or standard measures of association fail to capture the structure of the underlying problem.

Environmental & ecological science · Public health · Biomedical applications · Complex geometric data






My current research is developing a unified framework for differential and geometric inference over complex domains, while extending these ideas to increasingly large and dynamic datasets.



Intrinsic gradients, curvature, directional derivatives, and wombling for stochastic processes defined over manifolds.



Nearest-neighbor and scalable Gaussian-process methodology adapted to complex geometric domains.



Multiresolution representations for complex spatial and manifold processes, connecting local geometric structure across scales.



Statistical models for processes that evolve through time while being observed over non-Euclidean spatial domains.

title: Teaching
text:
My teaching emphasizes the connection between statistical theory and the computational tools needed to apply that theory to modern scientific problems. Across methodological and applied courses, I aim to develop both statistical understanding and the ability to translate that understanding into reproducible analysis.









GRADUATE



Computational methods and tools for modern statistical research, with an emphasis on implementation, reproducibility, and efficient statistical programming.

Drexel University · 2024–present





GRADUATE



Statistical modeling for spatially and temporally structured data, connecting Gaussian-process methodology with practical analysis and computation.

Drexel University · 2024





GRADUATE



Theory and application of generalized linear models, with emphasis on statistical inference, model formulation, diagnostics, and implementation.

Drexel University · 2025–present





GRADUATE



Foundations of statistical inference, including likelihood-based methods, estimation, hypothesis testing, and theoretical properties of statistical procedures.

Drexel University · 2026









Urban Health Collaborative Summer Workshop
An applied introduction to spatial and spatiotemporal data analysis using R, designed to connect statistical methodology with substantive problems in public health and related fields.

Drexel University · 2024–present




A twelve-week review covering core material in statistical inference and preparation for the doctoral qualifying examination.

Drexel University · 2024–present






Mentoring is an important part of my teaching. I work with graduate students through doctoral advising, master’s research, independent studies, and collaborative methodological projects.

title: Software
text:
I develop open-source software implementing methods from my research in spatial and spatiotemporal statistics, Bayesian computation, and statistical inference on manifolds.






FEATURED PACKAGE





nimblewomble provides tools for Bayesian wombling and boundary analysis using the nimble framework for hierarchical Bayesian modeling.
The package accompanies methodological work on Bayesian wombling and provides an accessible implementation for fitting models, conducting derivative-based inference, and identifying spatial boundaries.

R · CRAN · Peer-reviewed software


CRAN GitHub Paper












01



Gaussian-process derivatives on manifolds

Bayesian inference for spatial processes, intrinsic gradients, and directional derivatives over Riemannian manifolds.


R · Gaussian processes · Manifolds

GitHub →







02



Spatiotemporal wombling

Bayesian differential inference and boundary analysis for spatiotemporal processes.


R · Spatiotemporal statistics · Wombling

GitHub →







03



Spatial derivatives & wombling

Bayesian inference for gradients, curvature processes, and curvilinear boundary analysis.


R · Spatial statistics · Curvature · Wombling

GitHub →







04



Spatial Tweedie models & variable selection

Bayesian variable selection for double generalized linear Tweedie spatial process models.


R · Bayesian modeling · Spatial statistics

GitHub →








A recurring goal of my work is to translate new statistical methodology into software that can be used and extended by other researchers. These implementations also provide reproducible computational foundations for the methodological results presented in my publications.
